slice: The arctic fox and its snowfield (#775), the ibex and its crags (#782): the first two placeholder kinds of the cold north and the mountains made real, and the snow leopard's mock
built: The arctic fox (#775): a round white fox with a huge brush, its kit grey-brown and puff-tailed, its legend an aurora fox with three great tails glowing at their tips; it pounces like a fox mousing in the snow, and its legend's gift is Pounce. Its area, the snowfield: deep snow under groves of snow-laden firs and dwarf birch, a ring of old stones half buried in a drift

The ibex (#782): a stocky wild goat whose horns grow from nothing on the kid to great knobbled scimitars, its legend a glacier ibex with ice-tipped horns; it backs off and charges like the ram, and its gift is Sure-footed. Its area, the crags: lichened rock and glacier ice, rock spires, wind-bent larch, and (Ed: "even crags should have shrubs and maybe olive trees") broom, juniper and heather among the stones and a new tree, the wild olive
The set-piece generator takes an area's own colours over its genome's (`colour`: stone, dark, wood, moss, lichen), so the crags' rubble heap is cold grey; a heap with no moss has none at all
learned: The preview sheets are lit by a warm studio light, so a white coat or a blue-grey stone reads yellow or olive there; judge colours against a neighbour on the same sheet, or with NIGHT=1 as the game lights them
Every new area type used to reshuffle every seed's classic map and break the tests pinned to a seed; the journey's kinds now come only by their islands' rosters, so a new one changes no old map

With many builders adding animals at once, the same few lines (the area recipe list, the sigil neons, the movement bodies) collide on every merge: put new entries away from the others' where the file allows
